ImageDescription.value:
Disused Railway near Ballinhassig, Co. Cork
Ten miles from Cork, the Cork Bandon & South Coast Railway entered the Owenboy Valley and turned west. This is the old railway embankment, complete with telegraph poles, half a mile west of Ballinhassig station.

ImageDescription.value: Halfway Viaduct, near Ballinhassig, Co, Cork. One mile west of Ballinhassig station the Cork Bandon & South Coast Railway had to cross a gorge formed by a tributary of the Owenboy River. Sadly vegetation has encroached, restricting a good view of the three-arched viaduct.

ImageDescription.value: Upton station, Co.Cork. After following the Owenboy River west for some distance the Cork Bandon & South Coast Railway gradually turned south in order to join the valley of the Bandon River. This is Upton station which was midway between Ballinhassig and the town of Bandon.

ImageDescription.value: Castles of Munster: Ballea, Cork This tower house on a cliff above the Owenboy River was probably built by the FitzGeralds in 1439. Evidence suggests that it was remodelled in the early 17c as a three storey L-plan stronghouse. Occupied by the MacCarthys until the late 17c, it was in ruins by 1750 when it was restored by the Hodder family. It would appear to have undergone a modern restoration, and is now private residential accommodation.
